transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-31 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Romero, Priya Nair, Jonah Kim (Redwood) / Marcus Hale, Elena Cortez, Tom Briggs, Nadia Park (Silverlake)

Summary (auto): monthly check-in focusing on spikes, governance, pilot scope.

[00:00] Alex Romero: hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you all. we were going to run through the health signals you flagged and align on the pilot for dedicated capacity. can everyone hear ok?
[00:12] Marcus Hale: yep loud and clear. running a little late yesterday digging into the token surge, so appreciate the time.
[00:22] Elena Cortez: hi all, quick note, we care about tail latency on the long context routes, that was the main regression we saw after the last rollout.
[00:30] Priya Nair: got it, we'll pull logs for those longer sequences, sometimes kernel selection shifts when sequence lengths jump unexpectedly, that can bump p99.
[00:45] Tom Briggs: if you can point us to the logs that matter that'd be great, we only have limited visibility from our side because the proxy aggregates stuff.
[00:52] Jonah Kim: we'll attach the per-request latency traces, there's a trace id mapping in the console that you can enable for the next 48 hours.
[01:05] Nadia Park: also want to confirm encryption at rest and KMS rotation policy, our auditors asked for HSM-backed keys.
[01:15] Alex Romero: yes, we support KMS integrations, HSM-backed KMS is available via the private deployment offering, for hosted we have a managed KMS pattern, i'll include a matrix in the security pack.
[01:28] Marcus Hale: can you remind us the tradeoff? like if we go hosted with VPC vs private on-prem, what's the latency/cost delta?
[01:38] Priya Nair: generally hosted is fastest to onboard, cost efficient for bursty workloads. dedicated reserved pools give consistent throughput — you get better tail latency under steady load. on-prem/private gives you full network control and avoids egress but requires more ops. for your usage patterns with persistent spikes, dedicated looks attractive.
[01:58] Elena Cortez: dedicated pool sounds right but we're worried about unit cost — our finance team pushed back when we saw the committed number for Q3.
[02:06] Alex Romero: understood, we can model a hybrid: reserved baseline + burst-on-demand. we'll show the blended unit economics with examples from similar customers.
[02:18] Tom Briggs: can the routing policy fallback to a smaller quantized model if capacity hits the ceiling? we're fine with slightly lower quality for cold starts.
[02:28] Priya Nair: yes, smart routing can fallback to quantized variants; we can set per-route policies and automatic fallbacks with a confidence threshold.
[02:39] Marcus Hale: perfect. on the spike itself — what could cause that? we saw a 3x token day last week and can't explain it.
[02:48] Jonah Kim: a few possibilities — upstream crawler or new feature hitting longer prompts, concatenation of system messages, or retry storms. did you see any correlation with the customer-facing API gateway logs?
[03:02] Tom Briggs: gateway showed increased 5xx retries around 03:15 UTC, might have caused duplicate submissions.
[03:10] Elena Cortez: we also rolled a model change two days before, maybe prompts got longer inadvertently.
[03:17] Alex Romero: ok so action: we'll correlate Pine-ids (note: transcription sometimes garbles internal ids) with your gateway traces and share a root-cause snippet.
[03:29] Nadia Park: quick security question — retention of audit logs, we need 3 years of immutable audit logs for our compliance baseline. is that supported?
[03:38] Priya Nair: by default hosted has 90 days, dedicated can extend retention via the retention add-on, and private can be configured for multi-year immutable storage — we'll map cost for those tiers.
[03:52] Marcus Hale: that sounds fair. also want to understand SSO flow, we use Okta with SCIM provisioning — can we lock down RBAC per team and per-model?
[04:03] Alex Romero: yes, SSO with SAML/OIDC and SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC is token and role-based; you can scope model access to teams and restrict export/embeddings endpoints. we'll include docs.
[04:19] Elena Cortez: onboarding question — for the pilot dedicated pool, what's the minimum commit?
[04:25] Priya Nair: minimums vary by GPU type and region. for an initial pilot we often recommend a small reserved pool equivalent to two A100-class nodes or their AMP variants — it's flexible, we can tailor to your pattern.
[04:40] Marcus Hale: finance will want benchmark numbers though — per-token and per-hour tail latency. can you run a mirror load test?
[04:49] Priya Nair: absolutely, we can run a 2-hour load test and the harness will output token throughput, p50/p95/p99, and cost estimates. we'll want your synthetic prompt set and the evaluation prompts.
[05:03] Tom Briggs: timeline? we want this before the end of next week if possible.
[05:08] Priya Nair: i can coordinate and tentatively book next Thursday/Friday for the test window. i'll send the test checklist today.
[05:16] Jonah Kim: small note — when we run the load test we recommend enabling prefix caching for routes that use repeated system messages, that can reduce token cost by 20-40%.
[05:28] Elena Cortez: do you have any customers with similar prompt shapes? fractional examples would help our internal forecast.
[05:35] Alex Romero: yes we'll include anonymized benchmarks from a customer with long context and bursty traffic — we won't share PII but we'll show the delta switching to dedicated + caching.
[05:47] Nadia Park: about SOC2 — what's Redwood's timeline? we need a SOC2 report for an audit in Q4.
[05:56] Alex Romero: Redwood is SOC2 Type II in progress; i'll include the current attestation status and expected completion quarter. for immediate needs we can provide our security questionnaire answers and third-party pen test summaries.
[06:10] Marcus Hale: related — can we see sample audit logs and the schema? engineers need to map fields to our SIEM.
[06:19] Priya Nair: we'll share the audit log schema and a sample ingestion document — it's JSON lines with request id, model_id, route, token counts, latency, and decision flags.
[06:31] Tom Briggs: and retention controls? can we push logs to our S3 bucket?
[06:36] Jonah Kim: yes for dedicated/private you can export to your S3 or GCS, with lifecycle rules. hosted can ship to a secure customer bucket via cross-account role.
[06:48] Elena Cortez: back to costs — the variance last month surprised finance. can you show a forecast with a 95th percentile headroom?
[06:57] Alex Romero: we can produce a forecast with headroom bands and a recommended committed baseline. we'll show the blended cost with dedicated baseline plus burst.
[07:08] Marcus Hale: what about automatic right-sizing? can Redwood suggest quantization or smaller models for less-critical routes?
[07:16] Priya Nair: yes, Optimize suggests quantization profiles and model variants per route. it's driven by throughput vs quality experiments you run.
[07:26] Nadia Park: small compliance corner case — do you support customer-managed keys for embeddings storage? we store PII and want control.
[07:36] Alex Romero: for embeddings in hosted we encrypt at rest, but for customer-managed keys that's available in private/dedicated + the embedding store can be configured to use your KMS. we'll detail that.
[07:48] Elena Cortez: ok let's lock down success criteria for the pilot: 1) sustained p95 < 250ms for short routes, 2) p99 for long-context under 1.2s, 3) cost per 1k tokens within the blended forecast, 4) zero data exfil incidents in load test.
[08:07] Priya Nair: sounds good — we'll document the test plan and those KPIs.
[08:14] Marcus Hale: final ask from finance — can you provide a 6-month burn projection if we take the reserved + burst model?
[08:22] Alex Romero: yes we'll send a 6-month forecast with sensitivity bands (+/-20%).
[08:29] Tom Briggs: about the canary routing — if a rollout increases latency we want automatic fallback. how quickly can that happen?
[08:38] Jonah Kim: thresholds are configurable; we can set p99 latency + error thresholds with a 1-5 minute window and auto rollback to the previous model variant.
[08:49] Elena Cortez: any gotchas we should be aware of for long-context memory (kv cache consistency) when switching models?
[08:58] Priya Nair: switching models mid-session can invalidate KV caches, so we recommend session affinity for routes where the cache matters, or warming steps when you switch variants.
[09:12] Nadia Park: ok good. i'll compile a short compliance checklist and send it through.
[09:18] Marcus Hale: excellent. can we confirm pricing sheet will include a burst example and dedicated commit options?
[09:25] Alex Romero: yes, i'll include three scenarios: conservative, expected, and aggressive usage with cost per-1k token and committed discounts.
[09:35] Priya Nair: action: i'll follow up with a load test scheduling email and a test harness artifact.
[09:42] Jonah Kim: i'll drop the runbook excerpt and the canary config example.
[09:47] Tom Briggs: we'll send the synthetic prompt set and a mapping to real traffic patterns.
[09:51] Elena Cortez: and we'll confirm the pilot contact list and ops on-call.
[09:56] Alex Romero: great — thanks all. recap: security pack + pricing addendum, load test next week, runbook and KB snippets, follow-up in 10 days. i'll send meeting notes.

Notes about transcription: names occasionally mis-attributed, some technical ids redacted in transcript.

End of transcript.
notes: Redwood to anonymize benchmark examples before sharing.
Priya to prioritize p99 investigation for long-context routes before the load test.
